mechanism_inventory: external-call failure / DoS (unhandled revert from ZetaReceiver callback in onReceive/onRevert bricks delivery)
reentrancy via external callback (onZetaMessage/onZetaRevert called AFTER token transfer — CEI violated)
missing invariant enforcement — no cap on zetaValue/remainingZetaValue vs locked balance
access-control mismatch — send() emits ZetaSent with tx.origin not msg.sender (origin-spoofing/misleading trail)
wrong lifecycle ordering — token transfer before callback (CEI violation)
victim accounting direction — onZetaMessage revert leaves tokens transferred but message unacknowledged
hook caller/timing — destinationAddress attacker-controlled in onReceive; zetaTxSenderAddress in onRevert

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: CEI violation in onReceive: IERC20.transfer(destinationAddress, zetaValue) before ZetaReceiver(destinationAddress).onZetaMessage(...). Tokens transferred, then external call to same address; no nonReentrant on onReceive. Malicious destinationAddress can re-enter (e.g., call send()) before ZetaReceived event.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: TSS trusted (onlyTssAddress) but destinationAddress is TSS-supplied and can be any contract; attacker who controls destination (or in onRevert, the original sender) can exploit re-entry.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Deploy MaliciousReceiver R. 2. send() routes cross-chain message back to R. 3. TSS onReceive transfers V to R. 4. Connector calls R.onZetaMessage. 5. R re-enters send() with V, emitting phantom ZetaSent. 6. TSS may honor phantom send.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol locked-token accounting; destination chain may double-count.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker R extracts value on destination chain.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: CEI violated, no reentrancy guard, external-call target user-influenced — textbook reentrancy; at minimum creates phantom ZetaSent.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In onRevert, zetaTxSenderAddress (user-supplied at send() time) gets transfer then callback; user controls that contract; no reentrancy guard. Unprivileged sender obtains arbitrary callback with tokens already transferred.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged user who calls send() with a contract address.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Deploy ReentrantSender A. 2. A.send(V). 3. cross-chain reverts. 4. TSS onRevert transfers V to A. 5. A.onZetaRevert re-enters send() with V — phantom ZetaSent — potential double-spend.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: onRevert callback reachable by any original sender (permissionless); concrete reentrancy double-spend vector distinct from onReceive.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: send() records tx.origin in ZetaSent rather than msg.sender; when a contract calls send() for a user, attribution is the EOA, not the contract. Downstream TSS/authz relying on ZetaSent may misattribute the principal.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any contract integrating send(); tx.origin masks the intermediary.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. User U calls Aggregator. 2. Aggregator.send(). 3. ZetaSent emits tx.origin=U. 4. Downstream authz keyed on tx.origin enables phishing/front-running mismatch.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol integrity / users whose tx.origin is spoofed.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: tx.origin in cross-chain messaging is a known vuln class; different state (event attribution) than reentrancy.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Re-entrancy double-spend magnitude: whether TSS honors a re-entrant ZetaSent (replay/dedup on internalSendHash)
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: connector emits ZetaSent during re-entrant send(); TSS dedup behavior not in source.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does TSS deduplicate by internalSendHash/nonce? If yes, griefing/DoS; if no, critical double-spend.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: External-call failure DoS in onReceive if onZetaMessage reverts
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: onZetaMessage called with no try/catch; revert reverts the transfer too.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Can TSS retry? Does a griefing destinationAddress permanently lock a targeted message?

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: Missing cap on zetaValue vs locked balance — TSS over-unlock
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: onReceive/onRevert gated by onlyTssAddress; TSS is trusted accounting authority; ERC20 transfer reverts on insufficient balance.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Unprivileged attacker cannot call these; TSS compromise out of scope; balance floor exists.
rejected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol if TSS compromised (trusted by design).

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Potential double-spend of Zeta on destination chain via re-entrant send() during onZetaRevert/onZetaMessage.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Original tokens already transferred before re-entrant call.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Protocol locked-token reserve integrity; cross-chain accounting breaks if TSS honors phantom ZetaSent.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain supply conservation: locked tokens must equal circulating on destination; re-entrant send() after unlock breaks 1:1.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Re-entrant path permissionless (any send() caller / contract destination); impact proportional to zetaValue, not dust; only precondition is a cross-chain revert occurring.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: onReceive reentrancy, onRevert reentrancy, tx.origin spoofing carried; TSS replay protection + DoS finality unresolved
